subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the given sentence.

When he made fun of the sage, who was already infuriated, it __made a bad situation worse__.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Added fuel to the fire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Made them at loggerheads"** refers to causing two or more people to be in strong disagreement or dispute. (उन्हें गंभीर विवाद में डालना)

 
 
• **Example: **The debate over property rights made the two brothers at loggerheads for years.
 
 
 
• The idiom **"Added fuel to the fire"** is used to describe an action that worsens an already bad or volatile situation. (आग में घी डालना)
 
 
• **Example: **Commenting on the controversial topic on social media only added fuel to the fire.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate idiom for the given sentence is **'Added fuel to the fire'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Added fuel to the fire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Pulled someone's legs** (किसी का मजाक उड़ाना): Teasing or joking with someone in a friendly way.

 
 
• **Example:** They were just pulling your leg; they didn't mean what they said.
 
 
 
• **Budged up** (गलती करना): This phrase is not a standard idiom in English and seems to be a typographical error or a misinterpretation. Typically, "budge up" means to move over and make space for someone else.
 
 
• **Example: **Could you budge up a bit so I can sit down?
